title: Cris Pop on building a human-centric company: guidelines over rules and a meaningful day
summary: Cris Pop, founder of Thunder, explains why he builds a human-centric culture and runs the team with flexible guidelines instead of rigid rules. He covers strategy trade-offs, protecting deep work blocks, and refusing double standards between founder and team.

principles.text: Set strategy as flexible guidelines, not strict rules, so the team has room to explore, fail and adjust.
principles.quote: I usually try to have this strategy a bit of more like guidelines and less rules, because rules are very strict

principles.text: Accept you can't do everything; pick the best set of trade-offs and commit to it.
principles.quote: there is more work that I than I can do or like more work than the team can do.

principles.text: Aim for a meaningful day (a solid eight), not a perfect ten, to stay predictable and human.
principles.quote: I try to optimize it for having like a meaningful day rather than a perfect day.

principles.text: Do not expect every task to feel meaningful; accept unglamorous work as part of the bigger purpose.
principles.quote: We love it through the big picture cuz we understand it's an it's a needed piece of work so that we can do the whole thing we actually care about.

principles.text: Empower people to decide without waiting on the founder, and keep the same standards for yourself as for the team.
principles.quote: I don't want ever to have double standards in my team.

principles.text: Protect big uninterrupted blocks for creative work and group meetings instead of fragmenting the day.
principles.quote: You need probably bigger blocks of time, 3-4 hours, to just lean into that work and have no distractions.
